It describes Autopilot consent journal contention: independent provider sessions record consent concurrently instead of serializing behind the inventory write lock. It states that per-session ownership, account-erasure fences, and exclusive protection for identity merges and reward settlement are preserved. It also says canonical-machine ownership lookups are scoped to materialized ancestor IDs.

No code, authorization logic, attestation, encryption, billing, or configuration is visible in this batch, so no concrete regression can be asserted from it. The described implementation (a lock-granularity change) is not supplied. Relevant threat areas for a later pass that sees the actual code: T-060 (reward administration), T-059 (account erasure fences), T-055 (credential continuity vs. machine uniqueness), and TB-011/TB-006. Those passes should verify that concurrent consent recording does not race with erasure fences, identity merges, or reward settlement, and that consent observation cannot be attributed to the wrong canonical machine through the ancestor-ID scoping.

The changelog's claims are unverified because the implementing source is not provided. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
